- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overcorrects downward; delay or dampen the correction to allow for mean reversion.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending up, model may underreact; increase forecast slightly to capture momentum.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1st–3rd day) when sentiment is neutral or mixed; apply a small upward bias for first few days.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish, model often lags in adjusting; apply a 1–2 day lag correction to align with sentiment reversal.
- For long-term (15+ day) forecasts, model tends to overestimate mean reversion; reduce forecast by 1–2% per day after 10 days to reflect diminishing momentum.
